newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Independent Indonesian body says election unfair.
newsitem.headline: Independent Indonesian body says election unfair.

text.p: An independent Indonesian election monitoring group said on Monday that national polls this week would not be fair because they favoured the ruling Golkar party.
Asked at a news conference whether the election process was free and fair, Mulyana Kusumah, secretary-general of the Indonesian Election Monitoring Committee (KIPP), replied: "No."

Nearly 125 million Indonesians are eligible to vote on Thursday for 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives following a 27-day campaign that ended last Friday. The other 75 seats are reserved for the military which does not vote.
KIPP, set up last year ahead of the national and local elections held every five years, said in a statement it had recorded a number of violations during the campaign.

It did not give details except to say that state television had given Golkar with substantially more air time than the other two parties permitted to contest the elections, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
KIPP urged the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR), the country's highest constitutional body, to guarantee a democratic poll.
The MPR, comprising the 500 members of parliament and 500 appointed members, will meet next March to elect the president and vice-president and approve government policy.

KIPP also said violence during the campaign, which culminated in the deaths of more than 140 people in a shopping mall fire and riots in South Kalimantan province last Friday, was caused by social discontent among the people.
Three members of KIPP are currently in prison.

Budiman Sudjatmiko, leader of the small left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD), was sentenced earlier this month to 13 years in jail for subversion. Sri Bintang Pamungkas, sacked by the PPP as one of its members of parliament for outspokeness, received a four-year sentence for defaming President Suharto. Independent labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan is serving a four-year term for inciting riots . Reports by the London-based human rights group Article 19 and the Bangkok-based Forum Asia, received in Jakarta on Monday, described the election process as a sham and criticised what it said was government harrassment of KIPP.
